adds.title: High Court of Kenya - August 2025 transgender rights ruling
adds.summary: On 12 August 2025 the High Court in Eldoret recognized petitioner SC as transgender and affirmed transgender persons' right to self-identified gender and to legal recognition within Kenya's legal framework, holding state limitations on freedom from torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, equality and non-discrimination, dignity, freedom and security of the person, and privacy unconstitutional, and directed Parliament to enact a Transgender Protection Rights Act or alternatively amend the Intersex Persons Bill, 2024 and directed the Attorney General to explore amendment of Part VI of the Prisons Act to address threats to transgender persons in custody after finding prisons do not protect their dignity and privacy, and awarded SC KSh 1 million for dignity and privacy violations arising from her 14 June 2019 arrest at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital for 'personation' under Penal Code s.382 despite holding ID, birth certificate and passport with female sex marker, initial detention in women's police and prison facilities followed by degrading strip search, court-ordered gender determination implemented as non-consensual genital examination, radiology, hormone testing and blood sampling beyond the order, and leaking of private medical records to media, in a context where transgender persons face misgendering, forced undressing and invasive examinations without consent, placement in unsafe cells, denial of essential items and medication, and outing without permission in police stations and prisons.

adds.title: High Court of Kenya - 20 May 2026 gender-marker ruling - Audrey Mbugua lawsuit
adds.summary: On 12 August 2025 the Eldoret High Court recognized petitioner SC, arrested 14 June 2019 and charged with personation under Penal Code s.382, as transgender based on self-identified female gender, held that custodial strip-searches and non-consensual genital, radiological, hormonal and blood examinations and leaking of medical records violated constitutional rights to dignity, privacy, equality and non-discrimination, freedom and security of the person and freedom from torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, awarded Sh1 million damages, and directed the State to grant legal recognition of self-identified gender, enact a Transgender Protection Rights Act or amend the Intersex Persons Bill 2024, amend Prisons Act Part VI and provide appropriate police-station and prison facilities to protect transgender persons in custody.
